title: Use consumer-owned source-priority and cancellation leases
finding: The current preview path uses copied resident bytes or an isolated low-priority reader; playback preempts background reads and preview cancellation does not cancel playback. Shaka preview policies fork their network owner. Executed tests cover this supported ownership model, not shared torrent subscription leases.
novelty: R208 owns cancellation. Dropped R006 and R176 are rejected as dependency links; the proposal does not restore non-pthread or JSPI paths.
next_action: Retain isolated preview ownership. Introduce shared leases only for a requested shared scheduler and demonstrate overlapping consumers, stale verified blocks and independent cancellation; never seek/flush the main decoder for previews.
reopen_condition: Do not duplicate an already correct source scheduler. WebTorrent’s local iterator does not prove the scheduler’s overlap accounting; inspect that layer before adoption.

proposal_contract.Proposed mechanism: Attach requested ranges/groups, priorities and cancellation to playback, preview and inspection consumers. Releasing one consumer removes only its demand, not shared work still needed elsewhere.
proposal_contract.Smallest useful experiment: Overlap playback and preview reads, cancel the preview, replace the source and deliver a late verified block. Inspect scheduler selections and producer completion.
proposal_contract.Correctness gate: Playback continues; canceled consumers receive no stale data; shared verified data stays usable; no orphan demand/listener; unverified bytes never enter a trusted parser path.
proposal_contract.Measure only after correctness: Unnecessary fetched/verified bytes and cancel-to-quiescence time, preserving useful shared reads.

upstream_evidence: Imported 2026-09-21 source review, not fetched or revalidated in this run.
